cases.setup_script:
set -e
export TZ=UTC0 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null
export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=Fixture GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=fixture@example.test GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=Fixture GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=fixture@example.test
export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='2020-03-01T00:00:00Z' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='2020-03-01T00:00:00Z'
/usr/bin/ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -C fixture -f "$HOME/key"
/usr/bin/git init -q -b main signed
/usr/bin/git -C signed config gc.auto 0
/usr/bin/git -C signed config maintenance.auto false
printf 'signed\n' >signed/file
/usr/bin/git -C signed add file
/usr/bin/git -C signed -c gpg.format=ssh -c user.signingKey="$HOME/key" commit -q -S -m signed
/usr/bin/git -C signed -c gpg.format=ssh -c user.signingKey="$HOME/key" tag -s -m signed signed-tag
cases.script:
export TZ=UTC0 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null
read -r kt kk comment < "$HOME/key.pub"
printf 'fixture@example.test %s %s\n' "$kt" "$kk" > "$HOME/allowed"
/usr/bin/rm -f "$HOME/revoked"
git -C signed -c gpg.format=ssh -c gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile="$HOME/allowed" -c gpg.ssh.revocationFile="$HOME/revoked" verify-commit HEAD >"$HOME/revoked.out" 2>"$HOME/revoked.err"; rc=$?
if [[ $rc != 0 ]]; then echo 'missing=rejected'; else echo 'missing=accepted'; fi
if /usr/bin/grep -F 'ssh signing revocation file configured but not found:' "$HOME/revoked.err" >/dev/null; then echo 'warning=yes'; else echo 'warning=no'; fi
/usr/bin/rm -rf signed
cases.oracle: Pinned Debian Git 2.47.3 and OpenSSH 10.0: missing configured revocation file emits a warning and verifies a valid allowed signer; behavior observed in preserved r13 dynamic reference run.
cases.comparison: Missing revocation path only. Debian Git warns and accepts a valid allowed signer. This build stays fail-closed and rejects. That difference is deliberate. The r3 case that expected system Git to reject a missing file is retired.
